Partial gamma local dependence

Source: R/ld_partgam.R
RMlocdepGamma.Rd

Computes the partial gamma coefficient for each pair of items, the association between the two items given the rest score (the total score minus one item of the pair), to assess local dependence. With the result of RMlocdepGammaCutoff(), it tests each pair against simulations, by default with a bootstrap p-value corrected across pairs.

Usage

RMlocdepGamma(
  data,
  cutoff = NULL,
  p_value = NULL,
  correction = c("fwer", "fdr_bh", "fdr_by", "none"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  output = "kable",
  n_pairs = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'RMlocdepGamma'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'RMlocdepGamma'
knit_print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. Missing values (NA) are allowed, but only complete cases are used, so at least one is needed.

cutoff

Optional. Default NULL, the asymptotic test of iarm::partgam_LD(). Either of:

  • The full result of RMlocdepGammaCutoff(). This enables the bootstrap p-values (see p_value), and the caption reports the simulation settings.

  • Its $pair_cutoffs data.frame alone, with columns Item1, Item2, gamma_low and gamma_high. Pairs are flagged against the interval.

Either adds the columns Gamma_low, Gamma_high and a logical Flagged (TRUE when the partial gamma is outside the simulated interval, or with p-values when the pair is flagged).

p_value

Logical or NULL. Whether to flag on one-sided bootstrap p-values for excess positive local dependence (p_gamma, padj_gamma), as in RMlocdepQ3(). Each pair is tested once, on gamma_pair, the larger of its two rest-score directions, and the p-value is repeated in both tables. The asymptotic p-value and star columns are then dropped, and the simulated interval is kept as a reference. NULL (default) uses the p-values whenever cutoff is the full RMlocdepGammaCutoff() result, so a call without a cutoff keeps the asymptotic table. FALSE gives the behaviour before version 1.2.0. The interval is a poor decision rule, since over m pairs a width w gives a family-wise error rate of 1 - w^m (Johansson, 2026).

correction

Character. Correction of the bootstrap p-values across all pairs (before any n_pairs filter): "fwer" (default, Westfall-Young step-down), "fdr_bh", "fdr_by" or "none". Used only with p-values.

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1). A pair is flagged when its corrected p-value is below alpha. Default 0.05. Used only with p-values.

output

Character. "kable" (default) for knitr::kable() tables, or "dataframe".

n_pairs

Optional positive integer. Keeps only the n_pairs pairs with the largest absolute partial gamma in each table, largest first. Default NULL, all pairs in iarm's order. Values above the number of pairs keep all pairs.

x

An RMlocdepGamma object (the kable output), for the print methods.

...

Not used by print(). Passed to knitr::asis_output() by knit_print().

Value

  • output = "kable": an object of class "RMlocdepGamma", a list of two knitr_kable tables, direction1 and direction2. In both, the rest score is the total score minus Item 2, and the two tables list each pair in its two orders, so together they cover both rest-score directions. The columns are "Item 1", "Item 2", "Partial gamma", "Adj. p-value (BH)" and "p-value sign." (stars, as iarm shows them), plus "Gamma low", "Gamma high" and "Flagged" with a cutoff. In the console the object prints the two tables one after the other, and in a Quarto or R Markdown chunk it renders as two tables.

  • output = "dataframe": a named list of two data.frames, direction1 and direction2, with the columns Item1, Item2, gamma, se, lower and upper (95% Wald interval), padj_bh, Significance and gamma_pair (the larger of the pair's two directions). With a cutoff, also gamma_low, gamma_high and flagged. With p-values, padj_bh and Significance are replaced by p_gamma and padj_gamma, the same for a pair in both tables.

Details

Statistic. The partial gamma (Christensen, Kreiner & Mesbah, 2013) measures the association between two items after controlling for the rest score. Which item is subtracted from the total matters, so each pair is computed in both directions, which gives the two tables. Values near 0 indicate local independence, large positive values positive dependence (the items share variance beyond the latent variable), and large negative values negative dependence. The iarm package must be installed (it is in Suggests).

Asymptotic p-values. The adjusted p-value is a Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, made by easyRasch2, of the p-values from iarm::partgam_LD() over all \(k(k-1)\) tests in both directions. iarm's own adjusted column is a Bonferroni correction whatever method is named, since iarm adjusts one p-value at a time, so it is not used.

Bootstrap p-values. Each pair is tested once, on the larger of its two directions (gamma_pair), against its simulated values (cutoff$results, simulated under local independence and built from the same maximum). The statistic is the deviation from the mean of the observed and simulated values together, divided by their SD. The uncorrected p is one-sided for excess positive dependence (redundancy, as in RMlocdepQ3()), (1 + #\{t* >= t\}) / (B + 1) for B simulated datasets, so it can be no smaller than 1 / (B + 1). The interval still shows both bounds. correction = "fwer" uses the Westfall-Young step-down over all pairs, which uses the dependence between them (Westfall & Young, 1993, Ferreira, 2024). It controls the family-wise error rate at any number of iterations in RMlocdepGammaCutoff(), but below 400 decisions depend on the seed and a message says so. Use 1000 to 2000 for a final analysis. Unlike the asymptotic p-values, these are calibrated against simulations from the Rasch model. They depend on the model and the sample size, and are reported with the simulated interval, not instead of it.

Multiple comparisons

The uncorrected p-value controls the error rate of a single comparison. For one item (or item pair) chosen in advance it is the relevant value. Flagging whichever of k comparisons fall below alpha tests k hypotheses at once, and the chance of at least one false flag rises to about \(1 - (1 - \alpha)^k\), for example 34% for k = 8 at alpha = 0.05, even when every uncorrected p-value is calibrated. The corrected p-value controls this. correction = "fwer" bounds the probability of any false flag (strict, less power), and "fdr_bh" and "fdr_by" bound the expected share of false flags among those raised. Use the uncorrected p-value for a single comparison chosen in advance, and a corrected one when screening the whole table, which is the usual case.

References

Christensen, K. B., Kreiner, S. & Mesbah, M. (Eds.) (2013). Rasch Models in Health, pp. 133–135. ISTE & Wiley. doi:10.1002/9781118574454

Ferreira, J. A. (2024). Methods of testing a 'small' or 'moderate' number of hypotheses simultaneously. Journal of Statistical Theory and Practice, 19(1), 6. doi:10.1007/s42519-024-00412-4

Johansson, M. (2026). Simulation-based cutoffs for conditional item fit in Rasch models: Iterations, multiplicity correction, and decision stability. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/7pqz4_v2

Westfall, P. H., & Young, S. S. (1993). Resampling-Based Multiple Testing. Wiley.

See also

RMlocdepGammaCutoff() for the simulations, RMlocdepGammaPlot() for the plot, RMlocdepQ3() for \(Q_3\).

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("iarm", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(42)
  sim_data <- as.data.frame(
    matrix(sample(0:1, 200 * 10, replace = TRUE), nrow = 200, ncol = 10)
  )
  colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:10)

  # Default kable output
  RMlocdepGamma(sim_data)

  # Return as data.frame list
  RMlocdepGamma(sim_data, output = "dataframe")

  # Simulation-based cutoffs (use 1000 or more iterations in real analyses)
  if (requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cutoff_res <- RMlocdepGammaCutoff(sim_data, iterations = 100,
                                      parallel = FALSE, seed = 42)
    RMlocdepGamma(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res)

    # Bootstrap p-values with family-wise (Westfall-Young) correction
    # (use iterations >= 1000 in real analyses for stable p-values)
    RMlocdepGamma(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res, p_value = TRUE,
                  output = "dataframe")
  }
}
#> Bootstrap p-values are based on 100 iterations, below the recommended 400.
#> ℹ The family-wise error rate is controlled at any number of iterations. With few iterations the p-values are coarse, and which comparisons get flagged depends on the seed.
